state.name: auth

why: Origin, secret, and plugins come from authSettings. The remaining booleans and callbacks are the fixed sign-in and mail behavior, not caller settings.

state.name: auth

why: The await loads modules. The mounted third-party auth API uses graph-owned database and mail resources, creates no owned connection or timer here, and has no close API. Core owns its async build; ADR 0103 names the handler exception.

state.name: eventStream

why: Subscription, reader, close flags, and replay cursor are private protocol and IO lifetime state. Saved application records live in SQL and frontend cells.

state.name: eventStream

why: The stop listener sets ended and closes the subscription before async open work resumes. A body constructed after abort closes in start when ended is true. Pull also checks ended before reading or emitting. Existing opening-stop and held-stream tests cover both paths.

state.name: responseBodies

why: The reader Set and cancelled bit are private cleanup records behind the resource methods. No app view watches them and no listener set publishes domain state.

state.name: responseBodies

why: The synchronous factory starts no Core run that forced close must await. Stream pulls belong to the consumer; defer cancels pending readers and closes their requests. Consumer cancellation closes immediately. The pending-pull and scope-shutdown tests prove both paths.

state.name: responseBodies

why: The factory is synchronous and has no await. Its awaited stream callbacks finish or cancel owned work; after finish they check cancelled before emitting or closing. The added isResponse method only performs the same native instance check as the old entry.
